expectation: Membrane ring on a subset of small round lymphocytes (T cells), scattered singly in lamina propria and clustered in lymphoid aggregates, with some intraepithelial cells in gut; not on epithelium or other immune cells.
observed: A: diffuse yellow haze over the tissue with a bright rim at some edges. B: scattered small ring-like cells in stroma, with a hazy background. C: bright membrane-rimmed cells, some intraepithelial, around a crypt. D: clear ring-stained round cells. E: dense CD3E clusters, and CD4 cells sit on CD3E cells, though the CD3E signal is very bright and spreads wider than CD4.
why: Distinct membrane-ringed lymphocyte-sized cells appear in the stroma, in the epithelium and in aggregates, and CD4+ cells overlap them, despite a diffuse background haze.
notes: Membrane-ringed small cells are clear in B, C and D, including intraepithelial ones, and the aggregate in E is dense with CD3E+ cells that overlap CD4. Background haze is present, but a specific T-cell population stands out.
